test: none: the issue is open and has no fixing PR (SolidCraft's kernel work is paused, #3992), so `pr` points at the PR that adds this fixture, as the loader requires a /pull/ URL; the issue's property test (`crossing_cylinders_union_moved_far`, ignored) reproduces it; the numbers here are analytic
summary: The union of two crossing cylinders changed volume when both were moved by (1000, -700, 300) on SolidCraft's kernel: 2955.58 mm^3 at the origin and 2694.71 mm^3 moved (found by the `translation_invariant` property test; some tolerance does not scale with position). Cylinder A: base (17.5, 30, 7.5), axis +X, radius 5, height 10; cylinder B: base (17.5, 30, 15), axis +Y, radius 12.5, height 5. A comment on the issue adds the intersection of two parallel cylinders (A: base (7.5, 15, 5), axis +Y, radius 3.75, height 10; B: base (0, 10, 5), axis +Y, radius 11.25, height 7.5), 98.07 mm^3 at the origin and 110.44 mm^3 moved. For true cylinders the first union is 2893.4579 mm^3 (not the kernel's 2955.58), and in the parallel pair A lies inside B (the centres are 7.5 apart and 7.5 + 3.75 = 11.25, so the discs touch internally) over the y range 15 to 17.5, so the intersection is that piece of A, pi * 3.75^2 * 2.5. Each pair is run at the origin and moved, and both must give the same exact volume. The tolerance is 0.01 mm^3, as in the other boolean cases.

volume.formula: V = A + B - I; A = pi*5^2*10, B = pi*12.5^2*5; I = int_{17.5}^{27.5} int_{30}^{35} max(0, (7.5 + h) - max(7.5 - h, 15 - s)) dy dx, h = sqrt(25 - (y-30)^2), s = sqrt(12.5^2 - (x-17.5)^2) (B covers y >= 30 only, so half of A is inside its slab; z of B's disc below 15 - s); adaptive quadrature (scipy dblquad, error 5e-9) and 300 x 300 Gauss-Legendre agree within 1e-5; V = A + B - I
